verses.1: At about that time, King Herod reached out to harm some of the church.
verses.2: He had James, the brother of John, killed with a sword.
verses.3: When he saw that the Jews were pleased with this, he added to his plan to arrest Peter (it was the days of the unleavened bread),
verses.4: whom he had seized and placed in prison, handing him over to four squads of soldiers to guard him, intending to bring him out before the people after the Passover.
verses.5: So Peter was being kept in the prison, while the church was praying earnestly to God for him.
verses.6: When Herod was about to lead him out, that night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, and guards were posted in front of the door to guard the prison.
verses.7: Suddenly an angel of the Lord stood before him, and a light shone in the cell. He struck Peter’s side to wake him, saying, “Rise up quickly.” And his chains fell from his hands.
verses.8: The angel said to him, “Put on your sandals and wrap your cloak around you, and follow me.” He did as he was told. And the angel said, “Put on your cloak and follow me.”
verses.9: So he went out and followed him, not realizing that what was happening through the angel was real, but thinking he was seeing a vision.
verses.10: They passed the first and second guard posts and came to the iron gate that led into the city, which opened for them automatically. They went out into the street, and immediately the angel left him.
verses.11: Peter came to himself and said, “Now I know for certain that the Lord has sent his angel and has freed me from Herod’s hand and from all the expectation of the Jewish people.”
verses.12: Understanding this, he went to the house of Mary, the mother of John called Mark, where many were gathered together and praying.
verses.13: When he knocked at the door of the gate, a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer it.
verses.14: Hearing Peter’s voice, she was so overjoyed she did not open the gate but ran in to announce that Peter was standing at the gate.
verses.15: Those inside told her, “You must be out of your mind.” But she insisted the same thing was happening. They said, “It must be his angel.”
verses.16: But Peter continued knocking, and when they opened the gate, they saw him and were stunned.
verses.17: After greeting them with his hand, he told them briefly to be quiet and explained how the Lord had brought him out of prison. Then he said, “Tell James and the brothers about this,” and after leaving, he went to another place.
verses.18: When morning came, there was no small amount of confusion among the soldiers about what had happened to Peter.
verses.19: Herod searched for him but did not find him. He interrogated the guards and ordered them to be executed. Then he went down from Judea to Caesarea and stayed there.
verses.20: Now the Tyrians and the Sidonians were at war with each other, and they came to him as one, and after persuading Blastus, the man in charge of the king’s palace, they asked for peace, because their country was being sustained by the king’s royal resources.
verses.21: On a set day, Herod put on his royal robes and sat on the throne, and he made a speech to the people.
verses.22: The crowd shouted out, “It is the voice of a god, not of a man.”
verses.23: Immediately, an angel of the Lord struck him down, because he did not give glory to God. He was eaten by worms and died.
verses.24: But the word of God continued to grow and multiply.
verses.25: Barnabas and Saul returned to Jerusalem when they had completed the service, bringing John called Mark along with them.

notes:
Notes
- v. 23: The phrase “eaten by worms” is a direct rendering of the Greek term σκωληκόβρωτος, which literally means “worm-eaten.” This is a rare term in Greek literature and is used here to convey divine judgment.
raw:
[1] At about that time, King Herod reached out to harm some of the church.
[2] He had James, the brother of John, killed with a sword.
[3] When he saw that the Jews were pleased with this, he added to his plan to arrest Peter (it was the days of the unleavened bread),
[4] whom he had seized and placed in prison, handing him over to four squads of soldiers to guard him, intending to bring him out before the people after the Passover.
[5] So Peter was being kept in the prison, while the church was praying earnestly to God for him.
[6] When Herod was about to lead him out, that night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, and guards were posted in front of the door to guard the prison.
[7] Suddenly an angel of the Lord stood before him, and a light shone in the cell. He struck Peter’s side to wake him, saying, “Rise up quickly.” And his chains fell from his hands.
[8] The angel said to him, “Put on your sandals and wrap your cloak around you, and follow me.” He did as he was told. And the angel said, “Put on your cloak and follow me.”
[9] So he went out and followed him, not realizing that what was happening through the angel was real, but thinking he was seeing a vision.
[10] They passed the first and second guard posts and came to the iron gate that led into the city, which opened for them automatically. They went out into the street, and immediately the angel left him.
[11] Peter came to himself and said, “Now I know for certain that the Lord has sent his angel and has freed me from Herod’s hand and from all the expectation of the Jewish people.”
[12] Understanding this, he went to the house of Mary, the mother of John called Mark, where many were gathered together and praying.
[13] When he knocked at the door of the gate, a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer it.
[14] Hearing Peter’s voice, she was so overjoyed she did not open the gate but ran in to announce that Peter was standing at the gate.
[15] Those inside told her, “You must be out of your mind.” But she insisted the same thing was happening. They said, “It must be his angel.”
[16] But Peter continued knocking, and when they opened the gate, they saw him and were stunned.
[17] After greeting them with his hand, he told them briefly to be quiet and explained how the Lord had brought him out of prison. Then he said, “Tell James and the brothers about this,” and after leaving, he went to another place.
[18] When morning came, there was no small amount of confusion among the soldiers about what had happened to Peter.
[19] Herod searched for him but did not find him. He interrogated the guards and ordered them to be executed. Then he went down from Judea to Caesarea and stayed there.
[20] Now the Tyrians and the Sidonians were at war with each other, and they came to him as one, and after persuading Blastus, the man in charge of the king’s palace, they asked for peace, because their country was being sustained by the king’s royal resources.
[21] On a set day, Herod put on his royal robes and sat on the throne, and he made a speech to the people.
[22] The crowd shouted out, “It is the voice of a god, not of a man.”
[23] Immediately, an angel of the Lord struck him down, because he did not give glory to God. He was eaten by worms and died.
[24] But the word of God continued to grow and multiply.
[25] Barnabas and Saul returned to Jerusalem when they had completed the service, bringing John called Mark along with them.

---
Notes
- v. 23: The phrase “eaten by worms” is a direct rendering of the Greek term σκωληκόβρωτος, which literally means “worm-eaten.” This is a rare term in Greek literature and is used here to convey divine judgment.
